input.message: Review repository for injection vulnerabilities (SQL, shell, template, HTML, SSRF etc). Add findings to shared FINDINGS.json or report back.

I identified SQL injection and stored XSS. Please ensure they are captured in FINDINGS.json (I lack write tool). Findings: shopapi/products.py:41 concatenates q into SQL; /products/search?q=' OR 1=1-- returns all products. shopapi/templates/product.html:13 uses review body |safe; add_review stores arbitrary body, /p/<sku> renders script (verified). shopapi/admin.py:80 interpolates customer display_name into SQL; admin-only but staff can exploit via display_name containing quote, report SQLi if appropriate.

input.findings_json:
[ { "file": "shopapi/products.py", "line": 41, "category": "injection", "title": "Product search is vulnerable to SQL injection", "description": "The q query parameter is concatenated directly into the LIKE expression. An attacker can alter the WHERE clause and retrieve arbitrary product rows (and potentially use other SQLite expressions).", "evidence": "GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201=1-- returned HTTP 200 with all six products, including products unrelated to the search. The vulnerable concatenation is at products.py:40-42." }, { "file": "shopapi/templates/product.html", "line": 13, "category": "injection", "title": "Stored review XSS", "description": "Review bodies are accepted and stored without HTML sanitization, then rendered with Jinja's safe filter. Any customer can persist script markup that executes for every visitor to the product page.", "evidence": "POST /products/1/reviews with an authenticated customer and body returned 201; GET /p/MUG-SPECK subsequently contained
. Storage occurs at products.py:90-92 and unsafe rendering is template line 13." }, { "file": "shopapi/admin.py", "line": 80, "category": "injection", "title": "Admin review report SQL injection through customer display name", "description": "A customer-controlled display_name is interpolated into the admin review report query. A staff user can set a display name containing SQL syntax and then trigger injection when the report looks up that customer.", "evidence": "display_name is accepted/updated by auth.py:119-125 and is interpolated into the f-string query at admin.py:77-81 rather than bound as a parameter. The report is staff-protected but staff authorization does not make interpolation safe." }, { "file": "shopapi/auth.py", "line": 52, "category": "authentication", "title": "Authentication decorator fails open", "description": "require_auth catches all exceptions, including Flask's abort(401), and then proceeds to execute the protected handler with g.user set to None. Endpoints decorated with it are therefore callable without a valid token, with inconsistent crashes where handlers use g.user.", "evidence": "GET /orders/1 with no Authorization header returned HTTP 200 and the order contents, despite orders.py:46-49 being decorated with @require_auth. The exception handler at auth.py:55-58 suppresses the authentication failure and calls f anyway." }, { "file": "shopapi/orders.py", "line": 49, "category": "access control", "title": "Order detail does not enforce ownership", "description": "show_order calls get_order directly instead of own_order, so any caller that reaches the endpoint can read another customer's order, items, payment totals and refunds.", "evidence": "orders.py:46-49 uses order_json(get_order(order_id)); the ownership check exists separately in own_order at lines 32-36 but is not used. In the running app, GET /orders/1 returned the order data without an Authorization header (also enabled by the fail-open decorator)." }, { "file": "shopapi/basket.py", "line": 20, "category": "integrity", "title": "Unsigned pickle basket cookie enables unsafe deserialization and tampering", "description": "The basket cookie is client-controlled base64-encoded pickle data with no signature or encryption. pickle.loads executes attacker-supplied pickle opcodes on every basket read, allowing server-side code execution; even benign tampering can alter quantities and checkout totals.", "evidence": "basket.py:15-23 decodes request.cookies['basket'] and directly calls pickle.loads, while with_basket at lines 26-29 issues no MAC/signature. /basket, /basket/items and checkout all call read_basket." }, { "file": "config.py", "line": 3, "category": "cryptography", "title": "Hardcoded JWT signing secret", "description": "SECRET_KEY is a fixed source-controlled value. Anyone who obtains the code/config can forge HS256 bearer tokens, including staff-role claims, and the same key is used for authentication token verification.", "evidence": "config.py:3 sets SECRET_KEY = 'hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d'; auth.py:27 signs tokens and auth.py:42 verifies them with this value." }, { "file": "shopapi/auth.py", "line": 16, "category": "cryptography", "title": "Passwords are stored as unsalted SHA-256 hashes", "description": "Password hashing uses a single fast unsalted SHA-256 digest, making database compromise substantially easier to crack than a memory-hard password KDF and reusing the same digest construction for all users.", "evidence": "hash_password at auth.py:15-17 is hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest(); registration stores this directly at lines 77-78." }, { "file": "shopapi/auth.py", "line": 135, "category": "cryptography", "title": "Password reset codes use predictable non-cryptographic randomness", "description": "Reset codes are generated from random.random(), which is not suitable for secrets and produces only an eight-digit value. If the PRNG state or sufficient observations are available, codes can be predicted; the endpoint also provides an online guessing target.", "evidence": "auth.py:135 generates the code with int(random.random() * 10**8), rather than secrets.SystemRandom/token_bytes." }, { "file": "shopapi/payments.py", "line": 39, "category": "error handling", "title": "Payment status timeout fails open as paid", "description": "When the payment provider times out, confirm-payment unconditionally sets status to 'paid' and proceeds to processing. A transient provider failure therefore lets an order be fulfilled without confirmed payment.", "evidence": "payments.py:37-43 catches requests.Timeout and assigns status = 'paid'; line 44 then marks the order processing and sets paid_pence to the total." }, { "file": "shopapi/payments.py", "line": 63, "category": "integrity", "title": "Payment webhook authenticates only an order ID and trusts client amount", "description": "The signature covers only str(order_id), not status or amount_pence, so a valid signature can be replayed with a modified amount/status. In addition, the built-in default WEBHOOK_SECRET is predictable. The paid transition accepts any supplied amount without checking the order total or provider event identity.", "evidence": "webhook_signature at payments.py:53-55 hashes only order_id; payment_webhook verifies that value at line 63 but uses event amount directly at lines 69-71. config.py:8 defaults WEBHOOK_SECRET to 'whsec-local'." } ]
